resources.string: Spiral galaxy about 2.5 million light-years away. The marker and daily path follow its nucleus. M31* is a separate object; its mass is not the mass of the galaxy.
Central black hole of Andromeda (M31), a separate catalogue object. The mass and model horizon size refer to the black hole, not the galaxy.
Giant elliptical galaxy about 55 million light-years away. The marker follows its nucleus. M87* is a separate object; this photograph shows the galaxy, not the black hole horizon.
Earth is inside the Milky Way. The marker and path point towards the Galactic Centre, about 26,400 light-years away, not the entire galaxy. The panorama is an archival photograph.

Central black hole of NGC 5194 in M51, about 31 million light-years away. The marker follows the active nucleus. The mass of roughly 4 million solar masses is an indirect M–σ estimate with large uncertainty. The horizon is shown symbolically.
